course_title: Historical Perspective/ Europe Art Topics: Greek Myths through Images
subject: ARTHIST
course_description: The cultural context of selected traditions of European art and architecture, from ancient Mediterranean to eighteenth century, exploring the interplay of culture with historical circumstances. May be repeated when topic changes.
course_notes: (Same as CL 285 2) "Greek Myths through Images: The Art of Storytelling from Antiquity to Christopher Nolan"Zeus, Medusa, Achilles, Athena, Penelope, Odysseus: for thousands of years, these figures have starred in stories whose roots reach back to ancient Mesopotamia and whose branches stretch all the way to summer 2026, when Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey became one of the most talked-about, celebrated, and criticized films of the year. Why do these myths keep coming back, and what do they say about us? From Greek vases and Roman statues to Renaissance paintings and blockbuster films, this course explores how Greek myths have been imagined, transmitted, preserved, and reinvented through different visual media. Using methods from art history, Classics, and media studies, you will learn to read images closely as we trace how people have used and reused the same stories to express what they love, fear, desire, and hope for, to make sense of the world, and to connect with one another. Each unit centers on a specific myth, asking what it meant to ancient audiences and what new meanings it has taken on over the centuries. Classes combine lecture, discussion, and visits to the Michael C. Carlos Museum and the High Museum of Art in Atlanta. Art History major/minor: Division I
